### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, touching **1** documentable anchor(s).

**20** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 787d757405db4f3ebbc6ca811948af4438a3fe7a`.

⛔ **4** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.

Coarse fallback — **23** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 787d757405db4f3ebbc6ca811948af4438a3fe7a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `65ed2efc5a430799cc49eeccb011150d8e0101a0` — the merge of head `b41c3b24fffb93fe62a38c4d32be0b7658c8d443` into base `787d757405db4f3ebbc6ca811948af4438a3fe7a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 65ed2efc5a430799cc49eeccb011150d8e0101a0 && git checkout 65ed2efc5a430799cc49eeccb011150d8e0101a0
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 787d757405db4f3ebbc6ca811948af4438a3fe7a b41c3b24fffb93fe62a38c4d32be0b7658c8d443 && git checkout -B drift-repro 787d757405db4f3ebbc6ca811948af4438a3fe7a && git merge --no-ff b41c3b24fffb93fe62a38c4d32be0b7658c8d443

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 787d757405db4f3ebbc6ca811948af4438a3fe7a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 787d757405db4f3ebbc6ca811948af4438a3fe7a` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## ⚖️ 契约复审 **PASS** —— `needs:contract-review` 已摘(双载体同笔)

裁决全文与档位核验记录在卡侧:**#12297**(评论 `5480778427`)。摘要:

- **Clause-② 路径肢 `no`**(四个改动文件无一在 `packages/spec/src/**`)· **内容肢 `yes`**(`os lint --json` 新增 published `conversions` 键,含 caught-error 出口)· **申报诚实 `yes`**。
- **未改变接受/拒绝行为** —— `onConversionNotice` 默认 no-op、转换照跑,exit 语义与四项计数均有钉子锁住。
- CI 直读:35 个 check run,31 success / 4 skipped / **0 failure**(head `b41c3b24f`)。

**档位与核验(机读)**:本席自会话 `last_served_model` = `claude-opus-5`,`CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` = `claude-fable-5` ⇒ **不达档,⛔ 未自审**;经显式传 `model` 的 fable 子代理复审(上下文隔离、对抗性简报、⛔ 子代理禁写),转录 46 条 assistant 消息**全部盖章 `claude-fable-5`**、零回退证据 ⇒ 核验通过,**逐字采纳**。

⚠️ **一条 LOW,不阻塞**(裁决原文 "does not block, fix at will"):changeset 里 “`conversions` is **always an array** … can be read unconditionally” 的措辞比代码宽 —— `os lint --eval --json` 在 `runEval` 里于配置加载前短路,它的两个 JSON 出口都不带 `conversions` 键。代码行为本身站得住(那条路径什么都没算),建议措辞改成 “on every project-lint exit”,且目前**没有任何钉子标出这条边界**。⛔ 复审不把它列为返工要求。

⛔ **本条不代表已落地**:清标只是闸门放行。落地按 `landing-operations.md` 走落地前检 → 转 ready → 入队,本轮先向维护者呈报。

Reviewed post-merge (the PR merged at 2026-08-31T16:22Z while this review was in flight); the verdict was reached independently from the head tree (`b41c3b24f`) and is posted for the record. It concurs with the earlier PASS (comment 5480786046), including its LOW finding, which I rediscovered from the source before reading that comment's text as evidence.

**1. Is `os lint --json` a published/stable contract? Yes — by this repo's own working definition, though not schema-formalized.**

Found:
- `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx` (§ `os lint`, ~line 1292) publishes `os lint --json   # JSON output for CI` — a docs page pointing machine consumers at this payload.
- `packages/cli/test/json-stdout-purity.e2e.test.ts` states the doctrine ("`--json` has one audience — a program") and its `discoverFamily` docblock names `os lint --json` explicitly as a JSON emitter.
- Precedent grading: #13347 (`code`/`httpStatus`) and #12125 (`conversions` on `os validate`/`os build`) were both graded `minor` as additive members on a published machine-readable surface; this PR's changeset declares the same class in its opening line.
- `packages/cli/src/commands/validate-json-strict-exit.e2e.test.ts` already treats the sibling `conversions` field as payload contract.

Not found, with controls: no JSON Schema and no snapshot pin of the lint payload — `repo:objectstack-ai/objectstack path:packages/cli toMatchSnapshot` returned 0 hits, while the same index returned 14 hits for `"lint --json"` and 4 files for `path:packages/cli/src/commands "conversions:"`, so the zero is a reading, not a dead instrument. No ADR declares the CLI JSON payloads stable; stability is carried by docs, e2e pins, and changeset discipline. (`content/docs/releases/v17.mdx` also matched "conversions", but its hits are flow-node conversions — not this key.)

**2. Does an additive optional key widen the surface in clause ②'s sense? Yes.** A consumer asserting an exact key set observes the change, and the repo's precedent treats exactly this as a `minor` machine-contract widening. The gate flagged correctly, and the widening is done the way the precedent does it: the same `conversions` key and entry shape (`conversionId`/`surface`/`from`/`to`/`path`/`toMajor`/`retiresIn`) that `compile.ts` and `validate.ts` publish — both verified to carry `conversions: conversionNotices` including failure exits — unconditionally present, `[]` when empty, existing counts untouched, and pinned three ways (`Object.keys`, serialized bytes, value) in the new `lint-conversion-notices.e2e.test.ts`. Accept/reject behaviour is unchanged: `onConversionNotice` is a pure sink, exit codes are untouched, and the four counts are pinned equal across converting and canonical runs.

**3. Exit-path consistency — consistent on every exit of the payload it extends; the eval-mode payload is a separate family and does not carry it.** Exit paths in `packages/cli/src/commands/lint.ts` at head:
- `run()` JSON success/finding exit — `emitJson({ passed, …, conversions, duration })` (~line 612): key present.
- `run()` catch-all JSON exit — `emitJson({ error, …errorCodeFields(error), conversions })` (~line 701): key present, `[]` for a pre-normalize throw, per the 2026-08-25 ruling; pinned by the `earlythrow` fixture.
- Console exits: no JSON payload; the human face prints the notice and stays silent when nothing converted, both pinned.
- `runEval()` (`--eval` short-circuits before config load): its two `emitJson` sites — the generator-load failure and the report payload — do NOT carry `conversions`. That payload family never carried any project-lint key (`passed`/`total`/`issues`…), and no author config is normalized on that path, so emitting `[]` there would claim a check that never ran; the code boundary is defensible. What overruns it is the changeset's consumer note — "`conversions` is **always an array** on `os lint --json` … can be read unconditionally" — which is false for `os lint --eval --json`. Since `.changeset/*.md` is the input release notes are compiled from, that wording should be narrowed (e.g. "on every project-lint exit") in a docs-only follow-up, and a small pin marking the eval boundary would keep it honest. Non-blocking.

**4. The parity-guard widening is correct and reveals nothing left unfixed.** Verified the full assertion at head, not just the diff hunk: `validate-build-gate-parity.test.ts` requires a `normalizeStackInput(…);` match per file and `onConversionNotice` inside the matched call text. `lint.ts` has exactly one `normalizeStackInput(` call site (the import line carries no paren, so the first-match regex cannot latch onto it), the sinked call fits the 400-char window, and no second unsinked call exists for the regex to hide. The eval path calls no `normalizeStackInput` at the command layer, so it sits outside the class this guard enumerates.

**Verdict: clause ② applies and is satisfied.** Additive, precedent-shaped, consistent across the three authoring commands and across both JSON exits of the payload it extends, pinned on both faces. Follow-ups (non-blocking): narrow the changeset's "always / unconditionally" wording to the project-lint payload before release notes compile from it, and pin the eval-mode boundary.
